Verify Now Blog > HALO Grappleshot - Test Unit 1 Pneumatic Prototype (WIP) HALO Grappleshot - Test Unit 1 Pneumatic Prototype (WIP) by: MindForge Mechanics Oct 04,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in 3D Printing 3D printing CAD Grappleshot Summary： I’m building a functional HALO‑inspired grappleshot using 3D‑printed parts, pneumatic components, and a solenoid‑triggered air system. This project explores mechanical design, Fusion 360 modeling, and rapid prototyping with Creality Hyper PLA. It’s part of my STEM Regionals engineering build. Introduction This project is my first full electromechanical prototype of a HALO‑inspired grappleshot, designed for STEM Regionals and built under my maker brand, MindForge Mechanics. Instead of being a simple prop, this grappleshot is a functional pneumatic launcher built from 3D‑printed components, high‑pressure air hardware, and a solenoid‑controlled firing system. The goal of Test Unit 1 is to validate the mechanical design, air path, and trigger system before integrating custom PCBs in future versions. Video here! https://www.crealitycloud.com/post-detail/6ac471907 Project Overview The grappleshot uses a combination of 3D‑printed parts, stainless‑steel fittings, and regulated HPA air to launch a tethered hook. Every major component — the barrel halves, internal rails, latch system, hook housing, and shell — was modeled in Fusion 360 and printed using Creality Hyper PLA. This prototype focuses on: mechanical structure pneumatic pressure control solenoid‑triggered firing tether and reel planning early electronics routing Future versions will include custom PCBs for motor control, sensors, and optional LED indicators. 3D Printed Components All printed parts were made using Creality Hyper PLA (black) for strength and clean surface finish. Key printed components include: Barrel halves with internal guide rails Hook housing and tether mount Shell sections with mechanical ribs Internal support brackets Solenoid mounting block Regulator and hose stabilizers Trigger housing (mechanical version) These parts were printed with: 0.2mm layer height 3–4 walls 20–40% infill depending on stress zones Cooling optimized for dimensional accuracy Pneumatic System (Back → Front) The air system is the core of the grappleshot’s functionality. Test Unit 1 uses a regulated HPA setup to safely control launch pressure. Air Path Chain Maddog Aluminum HPA Tank (26ci/3000psi) ↓ HPA Low Pressure MR Reg GEN2 Micro Regulator (20–200psi) ↓ PTFE Thread Seal Tape ↓ TITAN Ultraflex Hose – 1/4" NPT, 36", 6,525psi ↓ SNS DC12V Brass Solenoid Valve (Normally Closed) ↓ ChillWaves 304 Stainless Steel Nipple – 1/4" NPT, 10" This chain delivers controlled low‑pressure air to the solenoid, which acts as the electronic trigger for firing. Electronics (Early Stage) Test Unit 1 uses simple wiring to power the solenoid: 22‑gauge wire Electrical tape for insulation Basic switch for manual activation Future versions will include: motor driver PCB trigger sensor PCB power regulation PCB optional LED status indicators optional wireless module These PCBs will be designed specifically to fit inside the grappleshot’s internal cavity. Tether & Reel System The hook is attached using: fishing line or paracord 6mm rods 6mm bearings small gears for reel planning The reel system is not fully implemented in Test Unit 1, but the mechanical layout is prepared for future motorized retrieval. Bill of Materials (BOM) Air System Maddog Aluminum HPA Tank – 26ci/3000psi HPA Low Pressure MR Reg GEN2 Micro Regulator PTFE Pipe Sealant Tape TITAN Ultraflex Hose – 1/4" NPT, 36", 6,525psi SNS DC12V Brass Solenoid Valve – 2W025‑N08 ChillWaves 304 Stainless Steel Nipple – 1/4" NPT, 10" 3D Printing Creality Hyper PLA (Black) Fusion 360 CAD models Printed barrel, shell, rails, latch, mounts Electronics 22‑gauge wire Electrical tape Basic switch DC power source Mechanical Fishing line or paracord 6mm rods 6mm bearings Assorted gears Future Plans Test Unit 2 will introduce: custom PCB integration motorized reel system improved shell design pressure‑optimized barrel geometry optional LED indicators full documentation for STEM Regionals Closing This project represents the first major step toward a fully functional electromechanical grappleshot for STEM Regionals. PCBWay’s community and resources have been a huge help in pushing my engineering skills forward, and future versions will rely heavily on PCBWay’s PCB fabrication and assembly services. Thanks for supporting young makers and helping projects like this come to life.
